title: Rosalind and the Crown
premise: Oscar Joubert has spent a decade erasing herself—trading her true name for the smuggler's trade and hiding her forbidden gift of swordspeech among the Thornfell passes. But when prayers start being answered by gods everyone thought dead, the court beneath the mountain wakes hungry, and Oscar learns her own soul was sold to it as a child in exchange for her survival. Guided by Rosalind, a priestess whose memories were stolen by the same bargain, Oscar must descend into the usurper's under-court to steal back what she paid. In the end, Oscar reclaims her soul but must surrender her invisibility forever: she speaks the old oath aloud before the free cities' armies, becoming the last swordspeaker no longer—and the first of whatever comes next.
about_author: Zephyrine Ashgrove is the pen name of a former cartographer who spent years mapping mountain passes across three continents before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who survive by forgetting, and lives somewhere she refuses to put on any map.

chapters.title: The Toll of Quiet Roads
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. She guides a cargo of contraband candles through the Thornfell passes, trading on her flawless memory of every smuggler's road while keeping her swordspeech buried. A dying pilgrim's prayer is answered aloud by something in the stone, and the mountain answers back to her blade. Emotional beat: unease—the world she hid from is waking.

chapters.title: A Woman Called Rosalind
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A half-remembered priestess named Rosalind finds Oscar at a waystation, insisting they made a bargain together years ago—one Oscar cannot recall making. Rosalind carries a ledger of souls sold to the under-court, and Oscar's name is written in it. Emotional beat: dread of discovering your own past is a locked door.

chapters.title: What the Blade Remembers
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. Pressed by pursuers from the usurper's inquisition, Rosalind forces Oscar to speak to her sword for the first time in ten years; the blade remembers her childhood and the night her soul was pawned. They flee into the deep passes together. Emotional beat: grief breaking through practiced numbness.

chapters.title: The Free Cities Will Not Fight
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Seeking allies, they reach the free city of Vaelmoor, where councilors weigh tribute against resistance and choose cowardice dressed as prudence. Oscar witnesses the usurper's herald demand every oath-bound child be surrendered. Emotional beat: bitter clarity—invisibility protected no one but herself.

chapters.title: Ledger of the Sold
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. In Vaelmoor's burned archive, Rosalind recovers fragments of her stolen memories and learns she was the one who brokered Oscar's bargain as a girl—a survival she engineered and then chose to forget. She confesses. Emotional beat: guilt, and the question of whether memory or mercy defines a person.

chapters.title: The Usurper's Road
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The usurper's armies close the northern passes; Oscar leads refugees along a road only she knows, spending her secrets like coin as soldiers hunt them. Her sword begins speaking unprompted, hungry for the oath. Emotional beat: reluctant leadership—the price of survival becomes the cost of others'.

chapters.title: Beneath the Mountain
chapters.summary: Rosalind's POV. The two descend through a drowned mine into the under-court, where the old gods sit enthroned and hollow-eyed, fed on sold souls. Oscar sees her own soul kept like a caged bird, still singing with her voice. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror at what divinity has become.

chapters.title: The Bargain Reopened
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Before the hollow throne, the god of debts offers Oscar a new contract: her soul returned if she swears her blades to the under-court and betrays the free cities. Rosalind offers herself in exchange instead. Emotional beat: the climax of identity—who Oscar is when every escape costs someone else.

chapters.title: Swordspeech
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar refuses both bargains and does the unthinkable: she speaks the full old oath aloud, unbinding her soul not by payment but by claiming it—every word of who she is, name and all. The under-court cracks; the caged souls scatter homeward as the mountain shudders. Emotional beat: triumphant self-reclamation at terrible risk.

chapters.title: The First of Whatever Comes Next
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Emerging to find the usurper's army arrayed against the refugee column, Oscar speaks the oath before armies and cities alike, and the awakened gods answer her—not as masters, but as witnesses. The free cities rise; Rosalind, memories returning, stands beside her. Emotional beat: resolution—an end to hiding, and a beginning neither of them planned.
